title: The Word 'Bootstrap' and the Paradox It Names
explainer: Computing borrowed "bootstrap" from a 19th-century idiom for an impossible feat - pulling yourself up by your own bootstraps - because a computer with no running program genuinely can't load one by itself. By 1953 the term had attached to the fixed sequence of instructions used to load a computer's first real program, and early machines like EDSAC solved the paradox physically, using hardwired stepping switches to feed in a tiny loader by hand before any software existed at all. The term is a reminder that every boot process, however automated today, is still solving that same chicken-and-egg problem.
